hypothesis.statement: The short-term DFA scaling exponent (alpha1) of RR intervals is HIGHER in elderly than in young healthy subjects (loss of fractal complexity with aging) on the real Fantasia recordings, and ecgDFA reproduces an independent standard-DFA implementation to machine precision.

analysis_plan.dataset: Fantasia (Iyengar et al. 1996, PhysioNet): young (f1y01-05) and elderly (f1o01-05) healthy subjects; RR intervals derived from the ECG (readWFDB -> ecgDetectRpeaks -> ecgRRintervals), physiologically filtered to 300-2000 ms

decision.threshold: descriptive: DFA alpha1 is higher in the elderly (aging_effect = old - young > 0), and ecgDFA equals an independent standard-DFA to machine precision (|diff| < 1e-9)
